question:
B. Is this measure already running in Lapland wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers. Invite 50-74-year-old long-term heavy smokers to low-dose CT with smoking cessation support, so cancers are found before symptoms. Finland is piloting this in 2026-2028.
effect_summary_en: A meta-analysis of nine randomised trials found 16% lower lung cancer mortality with low-dose CT screening (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.76–0.92).
supported_en: A 2021 meta-analysis of nine randomised trials in Lancet Regional Health – Europe found a pooled relative rate of 0.84 (0.76–0.92) for lung cancer death.
not_supported_en: The pages read do not confirm the NELSON baseline death rate of 3.30 per 1 000 person-years, and they give no results from Finland.
in_use_summary_en: No public sign of it in Lapland: the pilot that OYS and the Finnish Cancer Registry started in January 2026 is open only to residents of Uusimaa, Pirkanmaa, Ostrobothnia, North Ostrobothnia and Southwest Finland, and Lapha's screening page lists no lung cancer screening.
summary_en: OYS and the Finnish Cancer Registry started a lung cancer screening pilot in January 2026 for 1 200 long-term smokers aged 50–74, but only people from Uusimaa, Pirkanmaa, Ostrobothnia, North Ostrobothnia and Southwest Finland can apply. Lapha's screening page lists no lung screening. A meta-analysis of nine trials (Lancet Regional Health – Europe, 2021) found 16% lower lung cancer mortality (RR 0.84, 0.76–0.92), which matches the model's assumption.
unanswered_en: No page showed any plan to extend the pilot to Lapland or a national decision on a full screening programme.
